evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.text: Analyzes 桌 as 木 semantic plus 卓 phonetic, meaning a stand/table. Cites 正字通: “桌，呼几案曰桌.” Also cites an example from 兒女英雄傳, chapter 21, including 桌椅 and 一桌葷菜. The database describes 卓-derived “tall” as a possible motivation for the furniture name, but this is an account of the word’s naming, not proof that 桌 was first created by a semantic combination.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：桌

evidence.text: Describes the graph as 形聲, 从木、卓声; its detailed entry says “桌字本作『卓』” and reports later creation of 桌 with 木, also noting 棹 as a colloquial variant. The source does not provide primary evidence for when this graphic change occurred. Its account should therefore be treated as a dictionary explanation, not a securely dated formation history.
evidence.title: 桌 zhuō - 漢典

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.text: States that 卓’s graph-form origin is unsettled. It reports bronze forms, Warring States Chu manuscript forms, and seal forms; the Shang-era Shuowen analysis reads it as “high” and explains the graph as 早 plus 匕. The database presents a competing proposal that it may depict a person standing at a height, and names 张世超’s interpretation of the lower portion as 昜. Its interpretation is explicitly tentative. Shuowen’s proposed form explanation should not be treated as confirmed palaeography.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：卓

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.field: 卓—形義通解, citations to Shuowen and bronze inscriptions
evidence.text: Records 卓 in the Western Zhou Jiunian Weiding (九年衛鼎) and early Spring and Autumn Zhuo Linfu gui lid (卓林父簋蓋); it reports that the latter uses 卓 in the personal name 卓林父. Shuowen glosses the related headform 㔬 as 高也 (“high”). These early attestations establish the graph and an early personal-name use, not 桌 meaning furniture.
evidence.kind: dated inscription and historical dictionary report
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：卓

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.field: 卓—形義通解, 桌-related discussion
evidence.text: Reports the competing historical account that furniture called 桌 was written 卓 (also 棹), citing 《正字通》 and 《蜀方言》, and quotes a proposal by Zhang Shenhui and Qiu Xigui that 桌 developed from an old form of 卓. It also quotes the explanation that 卓 supplied the “high” sense for a high stand. The source gives this as scholarly discussion rather than a demonstrated sequence of dated 桌 graph forms.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：卓

evidence.text: Treats 棹 as a variant of 桌 for the furniture sense, citing 正字通’s “倚棹”/“倚卓” spellings and a report from 楊億《談苑》 that檀香倚卓 were made in the 咸平、景德 reign periods (998–1007). It distinguishes this use from 棹/櫂 meaning oar, a separate character history. This is secondary reporting of an early furniture term, not evidence that the graph 桌 itself was present then.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》：A01921 桌

evidence.source: 雅昌专栏 / 澎湃新闻, 张辉, 《中国家具史》 column
evidence.text: Reports that the name is later than the furniture: 楊億《談苑》 is cited for “咸平景德中，主家造檀香倚卓” with an explanation that 卓然而高可倚; it reports Southern Song 棹 forms in 朱子語類 and 建炎以来系年要录, and says 卓 and 棹 were both used through Song, Yuan, and Ming. It identifies the late-Ming 正字通 wording “桌，俗呼几案曰桌” as the earliest dictionary record known to that author. These are reported textual attestations; this source does not reproduce manuscript witnesses or establish that no earlier occurrence exists.
evidence.title: 张辉：唐宋时期局脚桌流变——《中国家具史》

evidence.field: 桌—康熙字典 quotation of 正字通
evidence.text: The entry quotes 正字通: “俗呼几案曰桌” (“tables/stands are colloquially called 桌”). Its cited wording documents a lexicographic characterization of the furniture sense; no publication date for the quoted 正字通 passage is supplied on this page.
evidence.title: 桌 zhuō - 漢典

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.text: Records a later classifier use: 桌 can count meals or people by tables, with an example from 兒女英雄傳, chapter 21, “一桌葷菜.” The source supplies no date for this passage on the character page; the classifier development’s chronology therefore remains undetermined here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：桌

evidence.field: 棹—詳細解釋; 康熙字典; 音韻方言
evidence.text: Separately records 棹/櫂 as a phonosemantic graph 从木、卓声 with the early dictionary sense “long oar”; cites 楚辭《九歌·湘君》 “桂棹兮蘭枻.” It also records later boat/paddle senses and a distinct furniture reading/use “倚卓也,” citing 楊億《談苑》 for 檀香倚卓 in 998–1007. The shared form and sound do not establish that the table word arose by borrowing the oar word or that one semantic development produced the other.
evidence.title: 棹 zhào、zhuō - 漢典

evidence.source: 中央研究院漢語多功能字庫
evidence.text: Reports Shuowen’s definition of 㔬/卓 as “high,” then cites early classical and later examples illustrating “standing out,” “surpassing,” and “tall.” This supports 卓’s independent semantic history; the furniture glosses of 卓/棹 are separately reported as historical spellings, so the senses should not be collapsed into one chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：卓

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.field: 桌 and 卓 sound comparison; repository cross-check
evidence.text: The host 桌 and sound component 卓 both have current Mandarin zhuō/zhuó respectively (the database labels 卓 as zhuó and 桌 as zhuō; exact tones differ in modern Mandarin). The local Baxter–Sagart table row checked for 桌 is: MC traewk; OC *tˤrawk (no pre-Qín exx.); gloss table. The supplied/local row for 卓 was not available in this input, and the official Unicode 卓 page could not be fetched during this research, so no Baxter–Sagart 卓 transcription is asserted. These limitations do not negate the dictionary’s explicit sound-component analysis; they limit the historical reconstruction comparison. Local row provenance: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, 桌 row; sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt, 桌 kMandarin row.
evidence.title: Unihan data for U+5353

evidence.text: Official U+684C Unihan record gives kMandarin zhuō, kFanqie 竹角, kDefinition “table, desk, stand,” and kJapaneseOn TAKU. This is current character metadata and dictionary indexing, not evidence for an ancient sound relationship. Checked local exact row: sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt, 桌 kMandarin=zhuō; sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, 桌 MC traewk, OC *tˤrawk (no pre-Qín exx.).
evidence.kind: official character metadata and local reading cross-check

search_audit.outcome: Targeted follow-up for textual chronology and 卓/棹 spellings. Inspected accessible newspaper/history article, official variant dictionary, and ZDIC. Shidianguji chapter fetch returned cache miss; several other results were search-result material only.

gaps: No pre-Qin examples for 桌 are reported in the local Baxter–Sagart row; available evidence does not establish a pre-Qin furniture sense or graph.

No independent pre-Qin attestation of 卓 used for furniture was verified. Reports place the related furniture term as 倚卓 in Yang Yi’s Song-era Tan Yuan (998–1007), with Southern Song 棹 spellings; exact original witnesses and earliest manuscript dates remain unchecked.

The claim that the 十 portion of 卓 merged with or was replaced by 木 is not established by the inspected sources. One dictionary says 桌 arose later with 木, but the historical form sequence and whether this was a graphic alteration, semantic differentiation, or folk/orthographic development remain unresolved.

The earliest-attested sequence of furniture senses is uncertain: accounts cite Song-period 倚卓/倚棹 but also state the graph 桌 is recorded by 正字通 in late Ming. A cited saying about the earliest dictionary entry is not a comprehensive corpus search.

The classifier sense ‘a tableful/one table of guests or dishes’ is attested in a cited novel example but its date and pathway from the furniture noun are not established in the inspected character-page evidence.

No 卓 Baxter–Sagart row was included in the provided local reading packet, and only the 桌 row was independently checked here. Do not infer 卓’s Baxter–Sagart form from 桌’s row or substitute Zhengzhang notation. Unicode U+5353 official record was attempted but failed to open.
The quoted pages list historical glyph images, but no glyph image was visually inspected. Graph-shape claims beyond page text and its cited reference listings remain unverified.
No source license or reuse grant was checked; no tracked source extract is recommended. Cite character-specific pages and use concise paraphrases.
